words.meaning: To add a code change into the main code.
A request to add a code change to the main code, so others can review it first.
To go back to an earlier version of the code or site.
A record a system keeps of what happened and when.
An on and off switch for one feature. It works without a new release.
The automatic step that puts the code together and runs every test.
A way for one program to ask another program for data or actions.
A secret code one program uses to sign in to another program.
A locked store for secret keys. Only allowed apps can read them.
To swap a secret key for a new one and turn the old one off.
Ready-made code from others that a project adds and uses.
To hide real names and details by swapping in made-up ones.
A small, urgent code fix released outside the normal schedule.
A set time when no new code releases are allowed.
Describes a test that sometimes passes and sometimes fails, with no code change.
A planned set of steps that changes how a database stores its data.
An organized store of data that apps read and write.
A sorted list a database keeps so searches run faster.
A database search that keeps typed text as plain data, never as a command.
A test copy of the live site, used to try changes before release.
A separate copy of the code where changes are made before they join the main code.
A teammate reads a code change and checks it before it is added.
A view that shows the exact lines added and removed in a change.
The steps to undo a change and go back to how things were.
You can look at it, but you cannot change anything.
